ideas.body:
Assume a partnership deed provides for interest on capital, but it is omitted from the accounts. The final accounts are prepared and profit is distributed before the omission is discovered. Arrange the following stages of the past adjustment in the correct order:
(A) Make the correction through the Profit and Loss Adjustment Account or directly in the concerned partners’ capital accounts, without altering the old accounts.
(B) Prepare the final accounts and distribute the profit.
(C) Calculate the omitted interest and determine its effect on the distribution already made.
(D) Discover the omission.
Choose the correct sequence.
A partnership firm has no specific agreement among its partners about the distribution of profits. Which rule governs this issue?

A partnership’s Profit and Loss Account has a credit balance representing net profit, and interest on capital is to be allowed. Arrange the following journal-entry steps in the order used to prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account:
(A) Allow interest on capital: debit Interest on Capital A/c and credit the partners’ Capital/Current A/cs.
(B) Transfer net profit: debit Profit and Loss A/c and credit Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c.
(C) Transfer interest on capital: debit Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c and credit Interest on Capital A/c.
Choose the correct sequence.

ideas.body: On dissolution, all the firm’s assets have been realised in cash for ₹6,70,000. The firm owes ₹3,20,000 to outside creditors.
